note: Wallachia maintained a complex relationship with the Kingdom of Hungary as a nominal vassal that frequently asserted effective independence. Hungarian kings claimed suzerainty over Wallachia as a buffer against Tatar and later Ottoman pressure; Wallachian voivodes paid tribute and provided military service intermittently. The Battle of Posada (1330) — in which Wallachian Prince Basarab I defeated Charles I of Hungary's invasion force in a mountain ambush — established Wallachian de facto independence. Mircea the Elder maintained a more cooperative relationship with Hungary as a counterbalance to Ottoman pressure, but never accepted permanent Hungarian control.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Battle of Posada (1330) is the founding event of Wallachian independence; the Hungarian-Wallachian relationship models the 'frontier buffer state' dynamic — Hungary needs Wallachia as a defensive zone; Wallachia exploits this need for autonomy while paying nominal tribute
